text:
A: Hello! Hi there. How's it going?
B: Yeah, fine. You?
A: Good, thanks. I'm Gareth. Last round, I think, we're nearly there.
B: Gemma.
A: Gemma! Are you the student nurse? I think about three people have mentioned you.
B: Yeah, probably. There's only one of us.
A: Ha. I'm a teacher, geography, in Maidstone. Head of Year 9 as well.
B: Oh, Kent. I grew up in Bexleyheath. Did my first degree in Kent.
A: No way, so practically a neighbour. Where'd you study?
B: Sport and exercise science. Then three years as an HCA, then this. So I'm a bit older than most of my cohort.
A: Nothing wrong with that. The ones who come to it late are usually the ones who really want it. That's my theory anyway.
B: Maybe. I just got bored of being an HCA and doing the same as the nurses for less money.
A: That's fair. Sport science, so are you sporty, then?
B: Netball. Tuesdays, when the rota lets me. Goal defence.
A: Nice. I do five-a-side on a Wednesday with a load of dads. We're trying to get a team shirt made, there's a whole WhatsApp war over the colour. And parkrun with my son, who beats me every week. He's eight.
B: Eight? That's embarrassing.
A: Thank you, Gemma, yeah, it is. Do you follow football?
B: Charlton, with my dad and brother. Sometimes.
A: Ah, I'm Gillingham. So we've both had a rough few years.
B: Yeah. I'd rather play than watch, to be honest.
A: Fair. What's the ward like? Acute medical, someone said?
B: Busy. Long days, nights. I'm knackered most of the time. I like it when it's kicking off and you've just got to get on. I don't like the paperwork.
A: Ha, the paperwork. I do mine on a Sunday night at the kitchen table, with the dog trying to eat the exercise books.
B: I've got an essay due Friday. Not started.
A: Friday! I'd be giving you a detention.
B: You can try.
A: Ha. Fair enough. What do you do to switch off? Holidays?
B: All-inclusive. Tenerife or Majorca. Sunbed, pool, done.
A: We're a campsite-in-France family. Drive down through the tunnel, kids moaning in the back.
B: That sounds like hard work, honestly.
A: It is a bit, yeah. You've caught me out there.
B: Do you do pub quizzes? You seem like you'd do pub quizzes.
A: Guilty. I'm the geography and sport one. Why, do you?
B: Now and then, with my husband's mates. I'm useless at—
